name: Eldaah
overview: Eldaah is a male biblical figure known primarily as the son of Midian and the grandson of Abraham through Keturah. His lineage places him within the extended family of Abraham, highlighting his connection to the patriarchal narrative. There is no further tribal affiliation or additional notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Eldaah means 'G-d [El] is [my] desire,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew understanding of God as El. This name is recorded in Genesis 25:4 and is not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Eldaah as the son of Midian, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no other family relationships are detailed except that he is a grandson of Abraham through Keturah.
scriptureSignificance: Eldaah's significance lies in his place within Abraham's extended family, representing one of the descendants through Keturah after Sarah's death. This lineage illustrates the breadth of Abraham's progeny and God's promise to bless his offspring. Although Eldaah himself does not play a prominent narrative role, his mention preserves the genealogical record important for understanding the fulfillment of God's covenant.
